analysis.evidence: וּלְשֵׁם means “and to Shem.” The verse names no child as the subject of יֻלַּד, but it identifies Shem as the ancestor of all the sons of Eber. English supplies “children” to express the implied offspring.
analysis.morphology: Pual perfect, third person masculine singular, used impersonally.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 67331:0, 66586:1, 66326:16, 66310:17.
הוּא refers back to Shem in וּלְשֵׁם. The preceding גַּם supplies “too,” so גַּם הוּא emphasizes that Shem too had children born to him.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun.
analysis.sense: he too; he and his company

analysis.evidence: אֲבִי כָּל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר identifies Shem as the ancestor of all Eber’s descendants. The phrase describes kinship across generations.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state. The final י belongs to the construct form אֲבִי.

analysis.evidence: In אֲבִי כָּל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר, “father of all the descendants of Eber,” כָּל includes the entire group designated by בְּנֵי עֵבֶר.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The verse calls Shem אֲבִי כָּל בְּנֵי עֵבֶר, “the father of all the descendants of Eber.” In this genealogy, עֵבֶר names the ancestor from whom those descendants trace their line.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name without a prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְּנֵי עֵבֶר, “the descendants of Eber.”
analysis.sense: Eber, the ancestor whose descendants are named here

analysis.evidence: The phrase אֲחִי יֶפֶת identifies Shem as Japheth’s brother in the genealogy.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state, with יֶפֶת as its complement.
